subject: general
question: Magnification produced by a spherical mirror is equal to ______.

options.text: Height of the image / Height of the object
Height of the image × Height of the object

solution:
The correct answer is __**Height of the image / Height of the object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnification is a measure of how much larger or smaller the image is compared to the object.
 
• It is defined as the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object.
 
• For spherical mirrors, magnification can also be related to the object distance (u) and image distance (v) by the formula: magnification (m) = -v/u.
 
• A positive magnification indicates that the image is upright, whereas a negative magnification indicates that the image is inverted.
 
• Understanding magnification helps in determining the nature and size of the image formed by mirrors and lenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spherical Mirrors**

 
 
• These are mirrors with surfaces that form part of a sphere.
 
• They can be concave (converging) or convex (diverging).
 
• Concave mirrors can form real or virtual images, whereas convex mirrors always form virtual images.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation**
 
 
• The nature of the image (real or virtual, upright or inverted) depends on the position of the object relative to the mirror.
 
• Understanding the mirror equation and ray diagrams helps in predicting the nature and position of the image.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Spherical Mirrors**
 
 
• Concave mirrors are used in reflecting telescopes, makeup mirrors, and headlights.
 
• Convex mirrors are used in vehicle rearview mirrors and security mirrors.
